backward_compat_traps.rule: DDR4 is 1.2 V; DDR3 is 1.5 V.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Driving DDR4 at DDR3's 1.5 V rail is wrong.

backward_compat_traps.rule: DDR4 has bank groups (BG0/BG1) with tCCD_S vs tCCD_L; DDR3 does not.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating DDR4 as flat-banked (DDR3-style) misses bank-group timing.

backward_compat_traps.rule: DDR4 multiplexes RAS_n/CAS_n/WE_n with A16/A15/A14 behind ACT_n.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Using DDR3's dedicated RAS_n/CAS_n/WE_n encoding is wrong for DDR4.

backward_compat_traps.rule: DDR4 is a single 64-bit channel with no DFE, no on-die ECC, and no DIMM PMIC; those are DDR5.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Applying DDR5 two-sub-channel / DFE / PMIC assumptions to DDR4 is wrong.

previous_versions_of_this_spec: DDR3 SDRAM (JESD79-3) — 1.5 V, 8 banks (no bank groups), external VREFDQ, no write CRC / CA parity / gear-down / DBI.

key_changes_vs_ddr2.impact: Ron and Rtt tracked to 240 Ω reference.
Termination strength changes for write bursts.

fields.version_naming_history_note: DDR4 SDRAM is JEDEC Standard JESD79-4, the fourth generation of the DDRx double-data-rate synchronous DRAM lineage (DDR -> DDR2 -> DDR3 -> DDR4 -> DDR5). DDR4 succeeds DDR3 (JESD79-3) and precedes DDR5 (JESD79-5), adding bank groups, gear-down, DBI, on-die VrefDQ training, write CRC, and CA parity while lowering the supply to 1.2 V.

key_changes_vs_ddr3.summary: VDD/VDDQ lowered to 1.2 V (DDR3 1.5 V); VPP 2.5 V added.
New BG0/BG1 addressing tier (4 BG x 4 banks = 16 banks for x4/x8) with short/long timings.
1/2-rate command/address capture for high speed bins.
DBI on DM_n/DBI_n to reduce I/O power and SSO noise.
VREFDQ moved on-die with controller-directed VrefDQ training (MR6).
Command/address parity (PAR) with ALERT_n persistent error mode.
ACT_n flag with multiplexed RAS_n/A16, CAS_n/A15, WE_n/A14.

future_versions_industry_outline.summary: Two independent 32-bit (40-bit ECC) sub-channels, decision feedback equalization, on-die ECC, on-DIMM PMIC + SPD hub, same-bank refresh, 1.1 V. DDR4 is a single 64-bit channel and does NOT have these features.
